o: From a single table of user permissions encoded as integers, compute the bitwise AND across all users (features everyone has) and the bitwise OR across all users (features anyone has). For permissions 5, 12, 7, 3 the AND is 0 and the OR is 15. This is a direct aggregation task.
k: MySQL provides BIT_AND and BIT_OR aggregate functions for exactly this purpose.
No grouping is needed — a single aggregate row over the whole table.

a.i: Aggregate functions BIT_AND and BIT_OR fold the bitwise operation across all rows, producing the two requested columns in one pass.
s: Select BIT_AND(permissions) as common_perms and BIT_OR(permissions) as any_perms from user_permissions.

w: If BIT_AND/BIT_OR were unavailable, you could emulate them with LOG/EXP tricks or a self-join reduction, but the built-ins are standard in MySQL. Empty tables yield NULL aggregates — consider COALESCE if that matters.
